title: Customer observability walkthrough + status update (Jan 28–29 2029)
content:
Purpose:
This is a customer-facing status update + short post-incident observability walkthrough intended for customers who saw elevated latency and occasional truncated responses across a subset of multi-region inference requests on 2029-01-28. The goal is twofold: (1) explain, in plain language, what happened and what we fixed; (2) provide an actionable observability checklist customers can use in future degradations so they can determine impact boundaries and short-term mitigations without waiting on operator updates.

Summary for customers (TL;DR):
- Event window: 2029-01-28 22:10 - 2029-01-29 01:05 UTC (majority of impact concentrated in first 40 minutes).
- What you saw: increased tail latency (95th/99th spikes), some streaming sessions stalled or truncated mid-response; a small percent of requests returned 5xx or timed out.
- Root cause (plain english): a change in routing heuristics combined with a transient KV-cache metadata inconsistency caused a set of routing decisions to send mid-length chat sessions to older model variants that did not support our streaming prefetch path. That mismatch produced stalls and network timeouts in the streaming path for affected sessions.
- Impact scope: ~1.6% of total requests globally; concentrated in EU-West and US-East regions and mostly affecting customers with sticky sessions and long-lived tokens.
- Immediate fix: we rolled back the routing heuristics change and orchestrated a targeted restart of the streaming gateway in affected regions by 2029-01-28 23:00 UTC; additional cache reconciliation ran, and the rate of errors returned to baseline within 55 minutes.

What customers will find in their Console/Status Page: (how to read the signals)
- Metrics to check:
  - Per-tenant 95th/99th latency charts (in Console > Metrics > Inference): look for a short spike that aligns with the incident window above.
  - Streaming session error rate (Console > Streaming): transient increase in stalls/truncations.
  - Model variant routing distribution (Console > Routing > Model Distribution): a shift showing more traffic to older model variants for the impacted timeframe.
  - Token-level traces (if you have tracing enabled): truncated response traces show the gateway hung while waiting on the streaming prefetch ACK.

Customer self-serve checklist (recommended immediate steps):
- If you saw user-visible errors/latency: try a soft client-side fallback for 10–20 minutes (reduce client concurrency, add exponential backoff with jitter, and show a lightweight placeholder to end-users).
- If you are using sticky sessions: consider temporarily disabling session stickiness for new sessions until you confirm routing distribution is stable.
- If you depend on strict streaming semantics: pin to a verified model variant in your deployment config (console or API flag) that we list as streaming-verified (see linked list in Console > Models).
- If you need an isolated replay: open a ticket to request a per-tenant replay window; include a sample request id and timeframe (we can surface preserved logs for 72 hours post-event).

Technical summary (for engineers):
- Sequence:
  1) At 22:08 UTC we deployed a routing heuristic tweak intended to bias short-prefetch scoring toward lower-cost variants. The change was subtle and targeted global routing tables only.
  2) At ~22:10 UTC a small but non-negligible set of concurrent sessions with long-lived tokens were rebalanced to model variants that do not support our new streaming prefetch handshake (race between gateway and KV-cache metadata version).
  3) The gateway attempted a streaming prefetch; the model variant rejected the handshake silently and the gateway entered a long-blocking wait -> resulted in stalls/truncations and upstream timeouts.
  4) Operators detected elevated stall metrics, disabled the heuristic rollout, and executed a targeted streaming-gateway restart + cache reconciliation.
  5) Traffic returned to baseline by ~23:05 UTC for most tenants; final clean-up and verification completed by 01:05 UTC.
- Root cause details: inconsistent metadata versioning between the routing layer and KV-cache after the heuristic rollout. The routing layer assumed a streaming-capable flag present in the metadata; the reconcile path that sets that flag was delayed during rollout (race window).
- Why the rollback fixed it: restoring prior routing behavior eliminated the path that chose streaming-incompatible variants for streaming sessions; restarts cleared the gateway wait states and forced metadata version re-sync.

Mitigations we implemented (short-term):
- Immediate rollback of heuristic and targeted gateway restarts in impacted regions.
- Accelerated KV-cache reconciliation job to re-sync metadata versions globally and force metadata propagation for sticky sessions.
- Added more aggressive health checks at the routing layer to detect streaming-capability mismatches and fail fast instead of entering long waits.

Planned longer-term actions (roadmap items):
- Stronger invariants between routing table updates and KV metadata (design doc in-flight).
- Safe-deploy gating for routing heuristics with canary traffic that simulates long-lived streaming sessions.
- Console improvement: explicit "streaming-capable" column in per-model metadata so tenants can quickly filter supported variants.

Customer impact and compensation policy (short):
- Impacted volume was small but we recognize user experience was affected for some customers. For any tenant who suffered measurable SLA breaches during the incident window we will evaluate on a case-by-case crediting offer according to our SLA policy. To request review, reply to this message or open a support ticket referencing INF-4723 and include tenant id and affected timeframe.

Suggested customer-facing status page snippet (short):
"We experienced a brief multi-region routing issue that caused elevated latency and occasional truncated streaming responses on Jan 28. We identified the root cause, rolled back the change, and restored normal operation within one hour. If you saw user-visible errors, please contact support and include a sample request id — we will prioritize investigations and replay options."

FAQ (anticipated customer questions):
- Q: Will my data be replayed automatically?
  A: No — we do not replay customer requests automatically. If you need a replay for reconciliation, please request it via support and we will coordinate (include sample request ids and tenant id).
- Q: Are my API keys or data exposed?
  A: No. This incident was a routing/streaming mismatch and did not involve data exfiltration.
- Q: Could this recur?
  A: We added short-term safeguards and are implementing longer-term fixes to reduce the risk. The rollout process for routing heuristics is being tightened.

Operational follow-ups for internal teams (short action list):
- Eng-serving-runtime: prioritize routing-metadata invariant doc and code changes (owner: Jonah Kim, due 2029-02-12).
- SRE: add health check that fails fast on streaming-capability mismatch (owner: Lina Morales, due 2029-02-05).
- Customer-success: reach out to top 20 impacted tenants with tailored incident notes and offer replay assistance (owner: Aisha Patel, outreach started 2029-01-30).

Notes and links for support responses:
- Linear ticket: INF-4723. Use this ticket id for any follow-ups.
- Slack incident channel: #incident-28. Operators and runtime leads are in the channel for coordination.
- Confluence: detailed technical postmortem + mitigation design sketch. Link above in the header.

Draft sign-off checklist (who must approve before publishing to the public status page):
- Eng-serving-runtime lead (Jonah Kim) — confirm technical accuracy.
- SRE lead (Lina Morales) — confirm mitigation wording and timeframe.
- Legal/Security reviewer (if requested) — confirm wording on data exposure.
- Head of Customer Success (TBD) — approve customer outreach tone and compensation wording.

Open questions (for triage during review):
- Do we want to offer a simple one-click tenant-level opt-in for limited replay windows in the Console? (product discussion)
- Should we include an anonymized example trace in the public postmortem to illustrate the failure pattern?

(End of draft)

Notes to self: keep language non-technical in the public status page; use this doc as the longer-form customer-facing note that we can paste into tenant emails. After approvals we'll produce a condensed statuspage entry and a tailored tenant outreach template.
